content: A diploma, derived from the Greek word δίπλωµα (diploma), is a formal certificate or deed issued by an educational institution, such as a university. It serves as evidence that the recipient has successfully completed a specific course of study or has been conferred an academic degree. In countries like the United Kingdom and Australia, the term diploma can also refer to a particular level of academic qualification. In these regions, such a document is sometimes referred to as a testimonium or testamur, which are Latin terms meaning we testify or we certify, reflecting the wording with which the certificate traditionally begins. In Ireland, this document is commonly referred to as a parchment. Historically, diplomas were crafted from sheepskin because paper was not durable and was challenging to produce. The sheepskin was processed to be as thin as paper, and the information was handwritten. Over time, parchment replaced sheepskin, and by the early 20th century, diplomas were often bound in leather. Initially, diplomas were quite large in size, but it has become standard practice to print them on letter-sized or A4 paper. In modern usage, the term diploma typically refers to the physical document received upon completing higher education. It can also denote a specific academic qualification. For example, in the field of nursing, a Diploma in Nursing was historically offered by hospital-based schools. In other parts of the world, the term diploma may refer to the education itself or indicate the duration of study. In some countries, such as Australia and India, a diploma represents a specific academic qualification that is of a lower rank than a bachelor's degree. In certain cases, an advanced diploma may exist as an intermediary qualification. For instance, a Diploma in Engineering (e.g., Electronics Engineering) is considered lower than a Bachelor of Technology in Electronics Engineering but is equivalent to a Bachelor of Science in Electronics. In Ireland, a National Diploma is below the standard of an honors bachelor's degree, while a Higher Diploma is pursued after obtaining a bachelor's degree. In Germany, Ukraine, and other countries that follow the German academic education system, the Diplom is a standard academic degree that is comparable to a combination of a bachelor's and master's degree. In Hong Kong, a higher diploma and an associate degree are qualifications below the level of an honors bachelor's degree. Certificates and diplomas in Hong Kong are ranked below higher diplomas and associate degrees. Postgraduate certificates and postgraduate diplomas, which are pursued after a bachelor's degree, are more vocationally oriented than a master's degree. In Ontario, Canada, diplomas are awarded by colleges, whereas bachelor's degrees are conferred by universities. In Canada, there is a nuanced distinction between colleges and universities. The International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma is a pre-university qualification typically undertaken by students during the final two years of high school. In the United Kingdom, the term diploma can refer to various types of academic qualifications. The Diploma of Higher Education is a higher education award that is below the level of a bachelor's degree. The term can also refer to a Postgraduate Diploma or the 14-19 Diploma, which was introduced in England in September 2008.
